name: Unit Utilization
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Mid-Term Planner
compared_against: plan (prompt schedule; short-term LP handover); prior plan version (mid-term vs short-term); last hour and last 24 hours
mpc_counterpart: MPC 2 (company crude utilization only; no unit figure published)
reason: A unit-level ratio of throughput to constrained capacity, watched by exception for units missing plan. Unit-level plant utilization sits in Gartner's Correct tier; no target or owner is recorded.

name: Crude Utilization
compared_against: submitted mid-term plan; same month in prior years (2 to 5 years)
mpc_counterpart: MPC 2 (crude oil capacity utilization, average calendar-day capacity)
reason: Crude unit utilization is the headline refining measure that MPC, EIA and Solomon report and that Phillips 66 targets, so it is the strongest candidate. It stays an operational metric until a target and owner are recorded. The planner's denominator (constrained capacity) differs from MPC's (average calendar-day capacity).

name: Current Plan vs. Historical Averages (Crude, Gas, Diesel, Jet)
reason: The submitted plan compared with history for the same month. A comparison of a plan with a reference, used to test the plan, not to score performance.

name: Distillate Yield
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner
compared_against: opening forecast plan; latest weekly schedule; short-term LP plan; distribution plan
reason: Distillate output as a share of crude and feed charged. MPC reports yields as operating statistics, not as key measures; no target or owner is recorded.

name: Gasoline Yield
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner
compared_against: opening forecast plan; latest weekly schedule; short-term LP plan; distribution plan
reason: Gasoline output as a share of crude and feed charged. Same reasoning as Distillate Yield.

name: Swing Stream Disposition
reason: A volume of swing streams that shape distillate and gasoline make. The calculation is still TBD in the list; the class holds if it is a volume per period.

name: Production Make (Clean Products)
mpc_counterpart: MPC 5 (yields); Phillips 66 clean product yield target
reason: Clean product output by refinery. Phillips 66 sets a clean product yield target, which would make a yield ratio a candidate at that company, but the list's measure is a volume with no target.

name: NGL Commodities (Plan, Consumption, Transfers)
reason: An NGL balance (opening plus production less consumption, plus or minus transfers) compared with planned purchases and make for the month.

name: Pipeline Utilization
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner; Mid-Term Planner
compared_against: distribution plan; mid-term vs short-term plan; 3 to 5 years of history
reason: Share of pipeline capacity used. MPC and MPLX publish throughput, not utilization, and no target or owner is recorded. The mid-term view also communicates constraints to MPLX.

name: Marine Utilization
personas: Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner; Mid-Term Planner
compared_against: distribution plan; mid-term vs short-term plan; 5 years of history
mpc_counterpart: MPC 31 (barge and towboat counts; no utilization published)
reason: Share of available barge and vessel capacity used. Actuals are not yet available in the prompt month.

name: Interregional Volume Totals
reason: Volume moved between regions per period, by product and mode. A descriptive activity measure (SCOR) used to see when movements must change.

name: Demand vs. Forecast
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner; Mid-Term Planner
compared_against: distribution plan; short-term LP plan; mid-term vs short-term plan
reason: Actual sales less forecast for one period. A single-period gap is a diagnostic (Gartner Correct tier). Forecast accuracy over many periods, with a target, could be a KPI (Gartner puts it top-tier as a driver); that would be a separate measure.

name: Supply vs. Forecast
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner; Mid-Term Planner
compared_against: distribution plan; short-term LP plan; mid-term vs short-term plan
reason: Actual purchases less forecast for one period. Same reasoning as Demand vs. Forecast.

name: Opening Inventory vs. Plan
reason: Actual opening inventory against the planned level, to judge what must change to stay within plan.

name: WoW Variances on DPO Input Tables
reason: Raised when an input table changes by more than X% week on week. It fires on a condition, so it is an alert, not a series.

name: Plan Overview and Key Changes
reason: A summary of the top changes and their economic drivers. It has no single formula, unit or grain.

name: Crude Value to Breakeven
mpc_counterpart: none (MPC names crude selection as a lever; margin capture is its after-the-fact counterpart)
reason: A crude-selection screen: each crude's breakeven value from the LP model against its delivered price, flagging incremental barrels for a full LP evaluation. It moves with the market and starts a decision; it has no target. Hamid asked for this to be researched (Part B, Q8).

name: Crack Spreads Pricing
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner
mpc_counterpart: MPC 10 (Gulf Coast, Mid-Continent, West Coast and blended 3-2-1 cracks)
reason: MPC files crack spreads under market indicators and calls margins dependent on factors beyond its control. The list's cracks (NYMEX 3-2-1, USGC 3-2-1 MEH ex-RIN, Chicago WTI 3-2-1 ex-RIN) are benchmarks, not performance.

name: Gasoline Market Pricing
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner
reason: Benchmark gasoline prices (NYH, USGC and Chicago CBOB). External market observations.

name: Distillate Market Pricing
personas: Prompt Planner; Short-Term Planner; Distribution Planner
reason: Benchmark distillate prices (NYH, USGC and Chicago ULSD; USGC jet). External market observations.

name: Crude Market Pricing
mpc_counterpart: MPC 11, 12 (crude markers; sweet and sour differentials)
reason: Crude benchmarks and differentials (Brent, WTI, Bakken at Patoka vs WTI CMA, natural gas, heating oil, RBOB). External market observations.

name: Price Comparison
reason: The difference between two chosen markers. A spread of two market prices is still a market observation.

name: Additional Market Prices (Benchmark, Crude, Renewables, NGLs)
reason: Further benchmark, crude, renewables and NGL prices. External market observations.

name: TAR Activities Tracker
reason: A list of turnaround activities for the next four months. The Mid-Term Planner's turnaround work is optimization of windows and sequence, not tracking (Part B, Q9); its measures are listed separately below.

name: Sales/Purchases Status Control
reason: A trend of rack sales and purchase statuses that stay in place for over a week. A status view, not a quantity with a target.

name: Production Rate Records
reason: A notification when a refinery sets a new clean products rate record. An event notification rather than an alarm, because a record is not an abnormal condition.

name: Capital Projects Evaluation
reason: Open project evaluations against due dates. Its linked alert (missed deadline, X days) is an alert; a count of late evaluations would be an operational metric.

name: MTP: Plan Submission
reason: Mid-term plan submissions against due dates.

name: Key Activity Tracker
reason: Critical activities and meetings against due dates.

name: Marketing Performance vs. Plan
reason: Marketing's results against its plan. Everything else about it is TBD in the list; the class follows the name.

name: Regional / Site Monitoring
reason: A future capability: one view of plant status with operations notes. Parked for a later phase.

name: Business Planning Data Trends (Ad Hoc / Chatbot)
reason: A future capability: ad hoc trends and a chatbot over the planning database. Parked for a later phase.

name: R&M Margin per Barrel
reason: MPC's non-GAAP realized margin per barrel of net refinery throughput, by region. A financial result measure (Parmenter's RI); MPC's bonus uses a related EBITDA measure instead. The definition changed in 2026 to include derivatives, so it is versioned.

name: Margin Capture
reason: Reported R&M margin divided by the R&M Margin Indicator. MPC calls it "an operations metric" and highlights it in the proxy, but sets no bonus target on it. It is the controllable measure built on the market indicators.

name: R&M Margin Indicator
reason: A hypothetical margin built from market data and MPC's operational guidance, posted monthly. Its formula is not published.

name: Refining Operating Costs per Barrel
reason: Excludes turnaround and D&A. A cost measure with quarterly guidance; not a named bonus metric.

name: Distribution Costs per Barrel
reason: Mostly MPLX agreements with minimum commitments, so largely contracted rather than managed day to day.

name: Planned Turnaround Costs per Barrel
reason: Expensed as incurred, so it rises in heavy turnaround years; an annualized cost (Solomon) compares years and peers more fairly. A turnaround outcome the Mid-Term Planner's sequencing affects (Part B, Q9).

name: Lost Margin from Turnarounds
reason: The margin given up for planned downtime: the quantity a mid-term turnaround optimization minimizes. Named in academic and benchmarking practice, not by MPC.

name: Relative Refining Margin per Barrel by Region
reason: An annual cash bonus metric (10%) with a target and accountable executives: MPC has designated it, so it passes test 5 on public evidence.

name: Relative Adjusted EBITDA per Barrel of Total Throughput
reason: An annual cash bonus metric (30%) with a target: MPC has designated it.
